description_full: PulteGroup, Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the homebuilding business in the United States. The company is involved in the acquisition and development of land primarily for residential purposes, as well as construction of housing; and sale of single-family detached homes; and attached homes, such as townhomes, condominiums, and duplexes under the Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, and John Wieland Homes and Neighborhoods brands. It also engages in the mortgage banking, title, and insurance agency operations. PulteGroup, Inc. was founded in 1950 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.
ceo_bio: Mr. Ryan R. Marshall | President, CEO & Director | Age 50 | Compensation: $6.3M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 6K people. Revenue per employee of $2.7M ranks in the top quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, improving at 9%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $269K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $8K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: PulteGroup, Inc. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $25.2B market cap on $17.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

The business throws off $1.7B in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.84× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
